value.body: A Commercial Pilot Licence (CPL) lets you fly aircraft for pay. It is a licence issued by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), not a university degree. You train at a DGCA-approved flying training organisation (or abroad, then convert the licence), log flying hours and pass DGCA ground exams. To fly an airliner you then need a type rating for that aircraft.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: There is no common entrance exam. You need Class 12 with Physics and Mathematics (students from other streams have cleared these through NIOS; DGCA has proposed easing this rule, so check the current position). Clear a DGCA Class 2 medical to start and a Class 1 medical for the CPL, then join a DGCA-approved flying school or an airline cadet programme.

value.title: At a glance
items: Training is largely self-funded and costly; ask schools for the full cost, including hours abroad.
A CPL alone does not get you an airline job; a type rating and airline selection come next.
The Class 1 medical has to stay valid throughout a flying career.
Training time often stretches because of weather, aircraft availability and exam slots.
